title: The Live Border
premise: Yara Ishikawa, a private security contractor hiding from his past, discovers that a voiceprint he buried years ago has unlocked a server in Lagos containing evidence of a sanctioned massacre. Hunted by the agency that trained him and pursued by a journalist who becomes his unlikely ally and love, Yara must decide whether to trade the server's location for his own safety or expose the truth. In the end, he chooses justice over survival, broadcasting the evidence at devastating personal cost, and finds a fragile new family among those who helped him do it.
about_author: Yara Okafor is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for private security firms before turning to fiction. Drawing on that world of encrypted dead drops and moral compromise, Okafor writes thrillers about people who discover their loyalties were never really theirs.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sleeps in Shifts
chapters.summary: Yara Ishikawa guards a paranoid tech executive in Geneva, running on four-hour sleep cycles since 'the incident.' His POV establishes his hypervigilance, his rules (no names, no attachments), and the tremor in his left hand he hides from clients. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the sense that invisibility is both armor and prison.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: A routine security audit pings an anomaly: a legacy voice-authentication system in Lagos has been triggered using a voiceprint matching Yara's own recorded testimony from years ago. POV shifts to Amara Diallo, an investigative journalist chasing the same signal. Emotional beat: cold dread — someone is resurrecting the past he buried.

chapters.title: The Incident, Retold
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Yara's POV: the botched extraction in Kivu, the orders he followed, the civilians who died, and the recording he made as insurance. He learns his old handler, Marcus Vane, knows the recording exists. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body in water; the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Yara burns his Geneva contract and goes dark, but Vane's cleaners reach the safehouse first. A brutal escape sequence leaves him indebted to a smuggler named Tomas, who owes him from another life. Emotional beat: adrenaline curdling into grief — the life he built is already ash.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Won't Quit
chapters.summary: Amara corners Yara in a Marseille safehouse, revealing she's traced the massacre's chain of command to a NATO-adjacent contractor called Meridian. They distrust each other intensely. Emotional beat: two predators circling, each recognizing the other's desperation.

chapters.title: What Meridian Buys
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Amara documents Meridian's shell companies while Yara infiltrates a data broker's office in Lyon. He finds proof Vane sold the operation's cover-up upward. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose — this is no longer survival, it's a case.

chapters.title: Tomas's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas agrees to move them toward Lagos but demands Yara's voiceprint authentication as payment — the very key to the server. Yara refuses; Amara argues trust is the only currency left. First real argument, first flicker of respect. Emotional beat: friction becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: A tense Mediterranean passage aboard Tomas's trawler. Vane's drone spots them; a near-miss forces Yara to reveal part of the incident's truth to Amara. She doesn't flinch. Emotional beat: confession as connection — being seen without being condemned.

chapters.title: Lagos Heat
chapters.summary: Arrival in Lagos; Amara's local contact, a retired archivist named Chidi, shelters them. Chidi knew the massacre's survivors. Yara confronts faces and names behind his redacted reports. Emotional beat: shame made flesh; duty and remorse colliding.

chapters.title: The Server Room Beneath the Church
chapters.summary: Chidi reveals the server sits under a mission church, guarded by a survivor militia who hate contractors like Yara. Negotiation scene: Yara offers not money but testimony on record. Emotional beat: humility as strategy; the first time he asks permission instead of taking.

chapters.title: Vane Arrives
chapters.summary: Vane lands in Lagos with legal cover and a kill order. He offers Yara amnesty and a new identity in exchange for silence, revealing Amara's editor sold her out. Yara stalls, shaken. Emotional beat: temptation — the old life offering absolution at the price of everyone else.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Amara learns her editor leaked her itinerary; she and Yara go deeper underground. Quiet chapter: shared watch shifts, a conversation about the families they failed. The found family forms around them — Tomas, Chidi, the militia. Emotional beat: tenderness inside danger; love admitted obliquely.

chapters.title: The Militia's Terms
chapters.summary: The survivor militia tests Yara: he must identify, from memory, the officers who gave the Kivu orders. He does, naming Vane among them. The militia grants access but keeps Amara as collateral until broadcast. Emotional beat: accountability accepted; trust earned the hard way.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Yara and Chidi enter the server vault beneath the church. The archive contains full operational logs, satellite imagery, and Vane's authorization signature. Copying it triggers a silent alarm. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed immediately by dread — they have minutes, not days.

chapters.title: Siege at the Mission
chapters.summary: Meridian's contractors assault the church compound at dawn. Tomas dies holding the gate; Chidi is wounded. Yara extracts Amara and the drive through the tunnels. Emotional beat: sacrifice and fury — the cost of truth paid in blood.

chapters.title: The Trade Offer
chapters.summary: Captured briefly by Vane, Yara is offered the final deal: the drive for Amara's life. Vane reveals the 'incident' was designed to test exactly this loyalty. Yara pretends to accept. Emotional beat: cold clarity — he understands now that Vane fears testimony more than bullets.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Yara turns the trap: he'd already seeded the archive with dead-man's-switch mirrors via Amara's press contacts. Vane's leverage collapses. A cat-and-mouse chase through Lagos's waterways ends with Vane's arrest warrant going public. Emotional beat: reversal and release — the hunted becoming the witness.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Amara publishes everything; hearings begin within hours. Yara gives sworn testimony, surrendering his anonymity forever, naming every officer including himself. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure — justice chosen over safety, fully conscious of the price.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Fallout: Meridian dissolves, indictments land, and Yara faces his own legal reckoning. Amara stands beside him not as an ally but as family. Chidi recovers; the militia's survivors attend the hearing. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting — victory measured in scars.

chapters.title: What the Night Holds
chapters.summary: Awaiting sentencing, Yara sleeps — truly sleeps — for the first time since Kivu. A quiet chapter of small repairs: letters written, debts acknowledged, Amara's hand in his. Emotional beat: peace as an act of courage rather than an absence of danger.

chapters.title: The Live Border
chapters.summary: Title chapter: Yara reflects that borders between duty and love, law and justice, past and future are live wires — you cross them changed or not at all. He walks out of the courthouse into Amara, Chidi, and Tomas's sister waiting. Emotional beat: arrival — the invisible man, finally visible and held.

chapters.title: Signal, Still Burning
chapters.summary: Epilogue, one year later: Yara runs a small firm training whistleblowers in digital safety, Amara publishing from the next desk. A new voiceprint ping arrives — someone else's buried truth, waiting. He answers the call. Emotional beat: forward motion — the arc closes but the work, and the family, endure.
